title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f: X -> S is smooth (later proper and smooth) in characteristic p, with relative dimension n. F^{(p)}_{X/S} is the relative Frobenius, and F^{(nu)}_{X/S} is its nu-th iterate (written (F_X)^nu when S = Spec F_p, where it is an S-endomorphism). The page belongs to the 'Cartier operation' part of the Gauss-Manin / Picard-Fuchs notes.

(1) Cartier as a transpose. The previous page defined F_X as an endomorphism acting on omega = f_*Omega^1. Here the endomorphism F^{(nu)}_* (a trace or Cartier-type operator) on f_*Omega^i is identified with the transpose, under relative Serre duality (X/S proper and smooth), of the pullback F^{(nu)*} acting on top-degree cohomology R^n f_*(Omega^{n-i}). Thus the Cartier operator on differential forms is Serre-dual to Frobenius pullback on the complementary Hodge group. For curves this is the familiar duality between the Cartier operator on H^0(Omega^1) and the Hasse-Witt map on H^1(O).

(2) Hodge sequence. There is the sequence 0 -> omega = H^{1,0} -> H^1_DR(X/S) -> R^1 f_*O_X -> 0, exact on the right in favourable cases (degeneration of Hodge to de Rham, base change).

(3) Compatibility. The Cartier operator on omega associated with F^{(p)}_{X/S} is compatible with the induced maps H^1_DR(X/S) -> H^1_DR(X^{(p)}/S) = H^1_DR(X/S)^{(p)}. These are endomorphisms when S = Spec F_p.

(4) Vanishing on the quotient. For X/S proper, the Cartier map on H^1_DR, coming from the conjugate spectral sequence H^1_DR -> H^0(H^1(F_*Omega^.)) = omega', has image in omega. Hence it induces zero on H^1_DR/omega = R^1 f_*O, up to transposition.

(5) Eigenvalues over F_p. Over S = Spec F_p, the eigenvalues of Cartier on H^1_DR are those on omega together with zeros. The nonzero ones are the reductions mod p of the Frobenius eigenvalues (l-adic, l != p, or crystalline) that are p-adic units. Grothendieck cites Katz for this; it is the unit-root / Hasse-Witt congruence (Manin; Katz, SGA 7 XXII).

(6) Continuation. The page then turns to forms with C omega = omega. The next page identifies these with logarithmic forms dlog. Their number is linked to eigenvalues congruent to 1 mod p and to dim_{F_p} of the p-torsion of the Jacobian. This is Serre's 1958 description of H^1_et(X, Z/p) via logarithmic differentials.
errors: The Serre-duality partner is garbled. Grothendieck (or the transcription) writes R^{n-i}f_*(Omega^{n-1}). Duality pairs f_*Omega^i with R^n f_*Omega^{n-i}; for curves, f_*Omega^1 is dual to R^1 f_*O. This looks like an index slip.
R^1 f_*(O_{X/S}) should read R^1 f_*O_X. The same holds for the H^{1,0} notation; these are cosmetic.
'Eigenvalues of l-adic Frobenius mod p' needs a choice of prime above p in the field of algebraic numbers involved. The statement is correct as a multiset in the residue field.

The claim continued on the next page is too strong. It says the dimension of {omega : C omega = omega} equals the number of Frobenius eigenvalues congruent to 1 mod p. In general the fixed space has the geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue 1 for the semilinear/linear operator, which is at most the algebraic multiplicity. Equality holds only under semisimplicity. The identification with dim_{F_p} of the p-torsion of J(k) is fine for fixed points of the Cartier operator.

ideas.what: Cartier operator on f_*Omega^i is the Serre-dual transpose of Frobenius pullback on R^n f_*Omega^{n-i}
ideas.modern_name: Duality between the Cartier operator and the Hasse-Witt matrix
ideas.where_published: Classical; the trace formalism is in SGA 4 1/2 / SGA 5 style; Katz SGA 7 XXII

ideas.what: Cartier operator on H^1_DR factors through omega and vanishes on R^1 f_*O; compatible with the Hodge sequence
ideas.modern_name: Conjugate filtration / Cartier isomorphism on de Rham cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (1970, 1972), Deligne-Illusie (1987) for the general framework
ideas.where_published: Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (IHES 1970); Katz, 'Algebraic solutions of differential equations' (Invent. 1972)

ideas.what: Nonzero Cartier/Hasse-Witt eigenvalues are the reductions of the unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Cartier/Hasse-Witt/unit-root material from the early 1970s, explicitly attributed to Katz on the page itself. It works out classical facts (Serre 1958, Manin, Katz) in Grothendieck's notation, with no new construction or connection.
transcription_corrections: 'R^{n-i}f_*(Omega^{n-1}_{X/S})' — the image is ambiguous; mathematically this should be R^n f_*(Omega^{n-i}_{X/S}), possibly a slip in the original.
'grâce[?]' is probably 'puisque' / 'parce que' introducing 'X est propre et lisse sur S'.
'R^1f_*(O_{X/S})' is in the original; it means R^1 f_*O_X.
'les = nous [?]' likely reads 'les homom. de Frobenius / induits' — illegible abbreviations for the induced maps.
